claims.assessment: Life-threatening systemic definition matches NHS/AAAAI/WAO.
Airway, circulatory and possible gastrointestinal manifestations are correctly distinguished.
No-rash caveat supported by AAAAI/ASCIA; food-testing source supports unpredictability and ACAAI venom material independently confirms previous reactions do not ensure future safety.
Mediator explanation is consistent with WAO pathogenesis and AAAAI patient teaching.
Named trigger examples align with WAO Table4 and AAAAI food/drug sources; no universal allergen warning.
ASCIA wheat-exercise FAQ explicitly explains combined cofactors, alcohol and NSAIDs; exercise alone is separately recognised.
WAO cofactors and AAAAI mast-cell source support risk modifiers without presenting them as certain causes.
WAO unexplained-reaction evaluation supports idiopathic disease and occult trigger/mast-cell investigation.
Clinical recognition precedes confirmatory testing; supported by emergency sources.
NHS/AAAAI/ASCIA agree on prompt prescribed-device use and emergency help.
Position is conditional on breathing/consciousness and concordant across NHS/ASCIA/WAO; no forced-flat breathing distress.
UK 5-minute repeat is accurately attributed; WAO clinician5–15minute advice is not presented as a contradictory universal patient rule.
RCUK CPR priority and ADAM/WAO resuscitation advice support not delaying compressions for medicine.
Practical ordering of emergency, observation and specialist care agrees with sources.
Default emergency/observation advice matches NHS/RCUK/ASCIA, including recurrence.
Risk-based observation and preagreed US help plans are scoped; FDA patient labeling and ACAAI support individual instructions, not self-triage during a first or worsening episode.
Isolated skin symptoms and progression warning are distinguished, without predicting that mild symptoms are safe forever.
Clinical emergency recognition is prioritised over testing.
RCUK record-keeping and allergy sources support exposure/timing history as a communication aid.
WAO/RCUK explain acute/baseline tryptase, timing and normal-result limitation; sampling cannot postpone rescue.
ACAAI/NLM support sensitisation-versus-clinical-allergy distinction and inability to predict severity from a panel.

findings.resolution: Added independently written WMS official summary corroborating RCUK no-induced-vomiting clause. WAO is retained only for trigger removal and immediate rescue; no false clause attribution.
Added Ontario professional Patient Management item9 as scoped corroboration of ADAM public breathing-difficulty instruction. Its BLS/ALS exceptions remain explicit; no universal oral ban is inferred.

evidence_boundaries: Independent editorial review is not clinician sign-off; medical_reviewed remains false.
RCUK, WAO, ASCIA and US allergy societies share clinical literature and endorsement pathways; distinct editorial authorship is not independent clinical trial replication.
UK five-minute injector repeat is explicitly attributed. US preagreed seek-help plans do not replace default emergency response for first, unclear, persistent or worsening episodes.
FDA-hosted label is manufacturer ARS labeling approved by the US regulator, not an independently authored clinical guideline; product instructions are used only within US prescribed-device scope.
Ontario evidence is a paramedic standard with protocol exceptions; ADAM supplies the public breathing-difficulty condition. WMS is a society summary, not a claimed full journal-guideline read.
Observation duration remains individualized. Low-risk record keeping and explanatory comparisons are not required to manufacture two independent efficacy sources.

WMS source was independently read from the same-session unmodified original web-tool capture after the source subsequently timed out/denied requests. This is not a claimed successful fresh network reopen or full journal-guideline read.
